newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pull back sharply at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pull back sharply at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks took a drubbing and closed sharply lower Friday on the back of a two-day rout on Wall Street, dealers said.
"The bolsa is prey to these sharp swings in New York -- until volatility fizzles abroad, we won't see a recovery," said Jose Napoli of traders Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index dived 2.3 percent to 661.95, posting its heaviest drop since December 12 and snapping a five-week winning streak.
The MerVal closed 2.8 percent lower for the week, paring January gains to 1.9 percent.

"Market conditions are overbought and favor this correction, but the medium-term outlook remains good," said Npoli. "The only real threat is a major shakeout on Wall Street, but that still seems pretty remote."
Traders said the bolsa was underpinned by steady economic growth and Argentina's successful launch this week of a 20-year, $2.0 billion global bond.

"The global bond is likely to become a benchmark for Latin America. I think Argentina will keep its edge compared to the other Latin markets -- it's a bit of a rising star," said an analyst at a foreign-based investment bank.
The broad market tumbled 2.5 percent Friday, with losers thrashing winners 44 to three and 13 issues closing unchanged.
Floor volume picked up narrowly from Thursday to 23 million pesos, while over-the-counter deals grew to 135.5 million pesos from 120.4 million Thursday.

Heaviest main-tier losers were Banco de Galicia, Telecom and textile firm Alpargatas, which reeled 5.0 percent, 4.2 percent and 4.1 percent, respectively. Real estate developer Irsa showed the only gain of 1.2 percent while petrochemical firm Indupa and construction stock both Polledo closed flat.
